nodes.label: Codex-boosted Full orchestration mode
nodes.rationale: LEAD = Fable 5 (frontier); Sonnet as workhorse, Haiku as fast scout, Codex (gpt-5.6-sol via ChatGPT subscription) treated as frontier-class for algorithmic work. Codex consent granted in the user's mission spec.

nodes.label: Pre-install Gate (2026-08-09)
nodes.rationale: Apple free-account install slots are scarce (3-app limit, 7-day expiry), so the ipa had to be proven phone-ready before consuming a slot: LEAD ipa forensics PASS, but blind verifier FAIL (unpinned fixes) and Codex FAIL (11 lifecycle findings) forced a DO-NOT-INSTALL decision and a batched fix wave before any install. Campaign consumed zero install slots.

nodes.label: FINAL-VERIFY campaign (515/515 tests)
nodes.rationale: Dual verification: Claude blind verifier PASS_WITH_NOTES (18/18 DoD rows, 1 LOW fixed) plus Codex cross-review (nominal FAIL from sandbox write-denials, no app defect; 1 MEDIUM sectorIndex finding fixed). Project verified at commit c3ca773.

nodes.label: App name decision: TRACE
nodes.rationale: User picked TRACE from 6 verified finalists produced by the Haiku naming scout; display name applied via CFBundleDisplayName while the bundle id stays frozen.

nodes.label: Bundle id freeze (app.circuittimer.tmr)
nodes.rationale: Bundle id frozen regardless of display-name choice because re-signing a sideloaded ipa with the same bundle id + Apple ID preserves on-device data and PBs across the 7-day re-sign cycle.

nodes.label: Per-group blind verification cadence
nodes.rationale: Blind verification is batched per integration group (core group, app group, final) rather than per micro-ticket — a deliberate cost/rigor trade-off logged as a decision.

nodes.label: WP-lifecycle outcome (TRACE-release-FINAL ipa)
nodes.rationale: All 14 pre-install findings fixed with sensitivity-proven tests (590 tests green), commit 361b708, CI build 31283955432 green, final ipa forensics PASS, install green-light delivered.

nodes.label: Expo Go dev-only / standalone on-track decision
nodes.rationale: User clarification: Expo Go is dev-only; on-track use requires a standalone offline iOS build installed from Windows (TestFlight paid path or AltStore/Sideloadly free path with 7-day expiry). WP14 must verify the TMR profile is statically inlined in the Hermes bundle and session paths make zero network calls.

nodes.label: Expo Go SDK 57 absent from iOS App Store
nodes.rationale: Expo is not releasing an SDK 57 Expo Go on the App Store (last approved version supports SDK 55 or earlier), which explains the user's 'version too new' error and forces the sideload path for both dev and on-track use.

nodes.label: Unsigned IPA route (expo prebuild + xcodebuild, no signing)
nodes.rationale: EAS Build device builds require a paid Apple account, so the free path is: expo prebuild, xcodebuild archive with CODE_SIGNING_ALLOWED=NO, zip the .app as Payload -> .ipa, then sideload.

nodes.label: GitHub Actions free macOS runners (public repo)
nodes.rationale: Public repos get unlimited free macOS minutes; private repos get 2000 shared minutes at $0.062/min for macOS (~2-3 iOS builds/month) — hence the recommendation to keep the repo public for the free build pipeline.

nodes.label: Free personal-team entitlement limits
nodes.rationale: Free Apple ID signing blocks push, iCloud, App Groups, and background modes, but the app's modules (expo-location when-in-use, expo-sqlite, expo-sensors, expo-keep-awake) need none of the blocked entitlements, so free sideloading is viable.

nodes.label: 7-day signature / re-sign cycle (free Apple ID)
nodes.rationale: Free Apple ID signatures last 7 days with a 3-app device limit; re-sideloading the same bundle id with the same Apple ID preserves app data, making a weekly ~2-minute re-sign routine the maintenance cost of the free path.

nodes.label: TRACE (naming candidate, 34/35)
nodes.rationale: Top-scored candidate: clean App Store namespace (no lap-timing app named Trace), premium telemetry positioning ('your lap's data trace'), one syllable, neutral in English and Romanian, no identified risk.

nodes.label: VECTOR (naming candidate, 33/35)
nodes.rationale: Runner-up: strongest technical premium feel, clean namespace; risk is abstraction — may not immediately signal lap timing without a tagline.

nodes.label: App Store name-collision analysis
nodes.rationale: WebSearch sweep of 11 shortlist names: Apex and Delta are high-risk exact collisions with existing lap-timer apps; Trace, Gate, Pace, Tempo, Vector, Lattice have clean namespaces; Sigma partially collides with SIGMA RIDE.

nodes.label: 1 Hz foreground GNSS constraint (expo-location)
nodes.rationale: watchPositionAsync at Accuracy.High delivers ~1 Hz foreground-only updates; this bounds achievable timing precision (~±0.3 s vs pro timing) and shapes every downstream timing/interpolation design.

nodes.label: Monotonic time rule (performance.now over Date.now)
nodes.rationale: Wall-clock timestamps can go backward on NTP correction; performance.now() is monotonic with microsecond precision, so durations/lap timing use it exclusively and expo-location timestamps serve only UTC correlation.

nodes.label: expo-sqlite WAL persistence pattern
nodes.rationale: WAL journal mode plus periodic (30-60 s) flushes handles the 1 Hz sample workload (~3600 rows/hour) and limits data loss across process death.

nodes.label: Battery/thermal envelope for 30-60 min sessions
nodes.rationale: Continuous high-accuracy GPS + screen-on costs 5-10% battery per hour and can push devices to 45-50 C; recommendation is Accuracy.High (not Highest) and expectation-setting in the validation checklist.

nodes.label: Process-death and state-restoration pattern
nodes.rationale: If the OS kills the app mid-session the in-memory buffer is lost but SQLite persists; AppState listeners plus periodic flushes are the survival mechanism that the checkpoint/recovery design builds on.

nodes.label: Security & privacy review report (0 CRIT/HIGH, 3 MED, 3 LOW, 6 INFO)
M1: circuit-profile array CPU-DoS
nodes.rationale: A hostile profile JSON within the 5 MB cap can pack ~80k centerline points and ~20k gates, driving O(gates x centerline) validation plus an O(gates^2) proximity loop (~1e9 ops) and a per-GNSS-fix full projection cost in TrackMatcher.match — latent until an import feature ships; fix is zod .max() caps and an O(n log n) neighbor check.

nodes.label: M2: unbounded in-memory session telemetry
nodes.rationale: rawSamples and pipelineCore's matches/rejectedSamples/stateHistory arrays grow one entry per GNSS fix for the whole session and are never trimmed; a multi-hour track day degrades memory and per-lap CPU on constrained iPhones. Fix: trim rawSamples to the in-flight lap and cap the diagnostic arrays with rolling windows.

nodes.label: M3: no user-facing location-data deletion path
nodes.rationale: deleteUserData is implemented correctly in sqlSessionRepository but never called from any screen, so precise driving-location history is kept indefinitely with no in-app removal; fix is wiring a Settings 'Delete my data' control to it.

nodes.label: L2: checkpoint deserialization validates envelope only
L3: unused expo-task-manager dependency
nodes.rationale: Declared but never imported; contradicts the foreground-only least-privilege posture and adds supply-chain surface for no benefit — removed until a background-location feature is deliberately decided.

nodes.label: Offline no-exfiltration posture (I3-I5 clean)
nodes.rationale: Zero fetch/XHR/WebSocket/axios call sites, no analytics or crash reporting, no console logging of coordinates, fully parameterized SQL, and least-privilege when-in-use location permissions — the review confirmed the offline-first privacy story end to end.

nodes.label: I1: iOS mock-location detection gap
nodes.rationale: Android mocked samples are dropped and counted, but expo-location exposes no iOS equivalent; a smooth spoofed track passes all checks. Accepted because the app is single-user local-only — impact is self-deception, revisit if sharing/leaderboards arrive.

nodes.label: Final Codex cross-family verdict ticket (fix wave 2 residue)
nodes.rationale: The reviewer who found the original defects re-judges fix wave 2 (F1-F6) against current code at 149e6f0, with an explicit SAFE TO INSTALL / DO NOT INSTALL output contract; test quality judged by reading since vitest may not launch in the Codex sandbox.

nodes.label: Final blind-verification DoD matrix (18 rows)
nodes.rationale: Adversarial fresh-context verification: every definition-of-done row (gates, TMR asset, calibration, matching, crossings, lap validity reasons, PB rules, live delta, offline audit, recovery, watchdog, security fixes, performance, docs, state machine, data provenance) must be reproduced from evidence, not the ledger; a row without evidence = FAIL.

nodes.label: Codex re-verification of fix wave 1 (C1-C11 + B1/B4)
nodes.rationale: Cross-family principle: the Codex reviewer who wrote findings C1-C11 verifies the Sonnet fixes are real and complete over git diff 7f892a4..361b708, hunting for fix-introduced regressions (its verdict: 5 PARTIALLY FIXED, 1 fix-introduces-new-defect, 3 NEW — still DO NOT INSTALL).

nodes.label: Pre-install adversarial lifecycle review (produced C1-C11)
nodes.rationale: Read-only hunt for defects that surface on the phone rather than in tests — lifecycle races, facade-swap subscription leaks, GNSS start/stop idempotence, recovery double-taps, backgrounding — because the user was about to consume a limited Apple sideload slot.

nodes.label: Mobile pure-TS vitest suite (WP-apptests)
nodes.rationale: Closes the app-side testing gap by testing only pure-TS session-layer modules (RealSessionFacade lifecycle, history store, settings store, circuitCatalog, LiveTimestampedLocationProvider, tmrProfile) against sql.js and fake clocks — no React rendering, no expo runtime.

nodes.label: Multi-circuit catalog (WP-catalog, createCircuitCatalog)
nodes.rationale: Typed catalog validating every raw profile through the existing loadProfileFromJson/validateProfile path at construction, keyed by (circuitId, layoutId); dependency-inversion friendly — the app supplies statically imported assets, the catalog never knows about Metro.

nodes.label: Final documentation set (WP-docs-final, 8 docs)
nodes.rationale: Algorithm docs (calibration, timing-and-crossings, live-delta), persistence model, testing-and-replay, known-limitations, privacy, and adding-a-circuit — each written against the actual implementations with an explicit instruction to report (not fix) implementation oddities, which surfaced the five WP-oddfix findings.

nodes.label: Real-track validation checklist (printable, TMR)
nodes.rationale: Physical validation protocol: GNSS rate and accuracy distributions, thermal over 30 min, calibration accept/abort behavior, pit-transit invalidation, 10-lap start/finish detection, stop-on-line, ±0.3 s agreement vs an independent timer, delta stability, PB replacement, backgrounding recovery, battery per 30 min — with a do-not-tune-to-one-device footnote.

nodes.label: Unsigned iOS CI + Sideloadly guide (WP-freeios)
nodes.rationale: Implements ADR-0005: a GitHub Actions macOS workflow producing unsigned Release and dev-client ipas (xcodebuild with signing disabled, scheme derived from app.json), generated ios/ folders gitignored per CNG, plus a beginner-proof zero-prior-knowledge Windows/Sideloadly guide covering the 7-day cycle.

nodes.label: TMR geometry verification packet (WP-geoverify)
nodes.rationale: SVG rendering plus numeric report (bounding box, S/F bearing, sector-gate fractions, pit-lane side, clockwise check via signed area) so the foreman can compare the shipped profile against the external racingcircuits.info reference layout; sanity assertions printed PASS/FAIL.

nodes.label: Pre-install fix wave 1 (WP-lifecycle, C1-C11 + B1/B4)
nodes.rationale: Foreman pre-decided the designs: fresh-controller factory + dispose for the one-shot controller (C1), inert PendingFacade bootstrap gate (C2), serialized GNSS lifecycle op-chain (C3), flush-before-save in endSession (C4), recovery-pointer re-point (C5), DevReplay facade restore (C6), lastError surfacing (C7), awaited background checkpoint (C8), keep-awake on Learn (C9), recovery lock + corrected copy (C10), cancellable preflight collectors (C11), PB-capture pinning test (B1), __DEV__-gated DevReplay (B4). Every fix gets a revert-detecting test.

nodes.label: Fix wave 2 residue closure (F1-F6)
nodes.rationale: Closes Codex's re-verification residue: subscribe-only-after-provider-start with state rollback (F1, the C7-regression called the most dangerous item the project has had), single in-flight preflight gate + dispose-finally (F2), facade activation only at full readiness + retryBootstrap (F3), locked replay transitions with flush-before-dispose (F4), vanished-checkpoint abort (F5), and DevReplay excluded from the release Metro graph via __DEV__ inline require proven by grepping the .hbc (F6).

nodes.label: Integration oddities fix wave (WP-oddfix, 5 findings)
nodes.rationale: Five verified-real wiring gaps surfaced by the documentation code-reading pass: corridorWidthM never wired into matcher/calibration, calibration-failure copy keyed to codes the engine never emits, GnssDiagnostics with zero UI call sites, the lifecycle onBackground checkpoint never registered, and lap numbering resetting to 1 after recovery.

nodes.label: corridorWidthM wiring defect
nodes.rationale: Profile declared 15 m corridor but TrackMatcher and CalibrationEngine each defaulted to 20 m independently; fix passes profile.corridorWidthM into both configs while keeping override ability.

nodes.label: Recovery lap-numbering defect
nodes.rationale: restoreFromCheckpoint built a fresh LapTimingEngine so post-recovery laps restarted at 1, colliding with restored historical lap numbers; fix seeds an initialLapNumber from max restored lapNumber + 1.

nodes.label: Matcher hinted-search optimization (WP-perf)
nodes.rationale: Confirmed finding: the matcher computed a full un-hinted projection on every call for hint-disagreement scoring, so hinted search saved nothing. Fix: full projection only on no-previous-match, lost mode, or a periodic audit every N samples (default 25), behavior-preserving, with benchmark tests asserting a >=3x measured ratio (3.67x measured) and throughput/memory guards.

nodes.label: Virtual replay time source (ScaledReplayClock)
nodes.rationale: Foreman-reproduced defect: 10x-accelerated replay re-stamped samples with the live clock, compressing inter-sample dt so the quality evaluator saw 10x implied speeds and rejected everything as IMPOSSIBLE_JUMP (calibration stuck at 8% coverage). Fix: a shared ReplayTimeSource virtual clock — samples stamped with virtual timestamps preserving original spacing, and a ScaledReplayClock implementing MonotonicClock injected into the controller; production GNSS path untouched.

nodes.label: Security fix wave (WP-secfix, M1-M3 + L1-L3)
nodes.rationale: Fixes all six review findings with tests: zod caps + 1 MB profile limit + O(n log n) gate check (M1), rawSamples trim + rolling caps on diagnostics arrays (M2), two-step inline delete-my-data UI wired to deleteUserData (M3), 10k acceptedPoints cap with CALIBRATION_OVERRUN failure (L1), per-lap checkpoint shape validation (L2), expo-task-manager removal (L3).

nodes.label: Straight-snapped sector gates (TMR layoutVersion 2)
nodes.rationale: Sector gates moved from exact 1/3 and 2/3 lap distance to the nearest low-curvature straight (curvature < 0.008 rad/m over a ±40 m window, within ±180 m of the target) so crossings happen on straights like real timing sectors; emitted deterministically as a v2 asset while the v1 asset stays untouched because PB keying depends on layoutVersion.

nodes.label: Independent security review ticket (WP-sec, read-only)
nodes.rationale: Read-only advisory review of first-party code at the owner's request: hostile profile JSON DoS, telemetry bounds, privacy/deletion completeness, permission posture, SQL injection, supply chain, unsafe deserialization, and GNSS spoofing denial-of-accuracy.

nodes.label: Endurance/adversarial soak suite (WP-soak)
nodes.rationale: The 'will it survive a real track day' suite on the real TMR v2 profile: 90-min 20+-lap session, multi-session PB carryover, recovery torture with process death, seeded GNSS chaos laps, watchdog gap storms, calibration marathon, delta NaN/stability soak, and SQLite growth + deleteUserData-leaves-zero-rows checks — deterministic, under 60 s runtime.

nodes.label: WP UI Redesign Task
nodes.rationale: Current UI reads cheap/AI-generated (generic blue accent, default system font, centered text); replace with a restrained, technical, motorsport-telemetry aesthetic. Dark theme stays.

nodes.label: TRACE dark palette (near-black + racing amber #FFB300)
nodes.rationale: Layered near-blacks with racing amber accent; semantic colors (delta green/red) reserved strictly for telemetry meaning to avoid confusion; no blue anywhere to break from the generic look.

nodes.label: TRACE typography system (Space Grotesk / Inter / JetBrains Mono)
nodes.rationale: Display/headings in Space Grotesk, body/UI in Inter, ALL timing digits in JetBrains Mono with tabular-nums for consistent telemetry-readable digit width; splash-gate prevents system-font flash.

nodes.label: Legal/ODbL attribution relocation off S1
nodes.rationale: ODbL attribution + geometry-provenance note + advisory disclaimer moved to Settings About section and CircuitDetailScreen so the circuit-selection list stays clean while compliance obligations remain always reachable.

nodes.label: WP Wordmark Task
nodes.rationale: Turn the S1 header into a proper TRACE brand hero, visually in-theme with the logo (metallic silver + glowing amber telemetry gradient on near-black); tasteful and premium, not flashy.

nodes.label: Telemetry-line motif (gradient bar under wordmark)
nodes.rationale: A thin horizontal amber-to-transparent gradient bar echoes the logo's glowing trace; kept subtle, no animation, so it reads as restrained rather than flashy.

nodes.label: MaskedView unavailable fallback (solid accent text)
nodes.rationale: MaskedView can be unavailable at runtime on web; the wordmark must feature-detect and degrade to solid accent-colored text rather than crash.

nodes.label: WP10 Replay Harness Task
nodes.rationale: The harness must compose the REAL production modules end-to-end (quality -> matcher -> crossings -> state machine -> lap/sector timing -> live delta) as proof the whole core works, not a toy timing implementation.

nodes.label: Seeded LCG/xorshift PRNG utility
nodes.rationale: Determinism required for byte-identical replay results: NO Math.random/Date.now allowed anywhere in fixtures.

nodes.label: Adversarial scenario fixture catalog (noisyGpsLap, signalLossLap, impossibleJumpLap, pitLaneTransitLap, etc.)
WP11a Persistence Core Task
nodes.rationale: In-memory LocalSessionRepository is both the test double the whole suite relies on AND the semantic reference the later SQLite adapter must match.

nodes.label: Atomic PB replace semantics (putReferenceLap)
nodes.rationale: A failed/partial write must be impossible by construction; structural validation of ReferenceLap happens before storing so a corrupt reference is never persisted.

nodes.label: Deep-copy read semantics (getReferenceLap)
nodes.rationale: Mutation of a returned object must never affect the store; enforced and tested via deep copy on every read.

nodes.label: WP11b SQLite Adapter Task
nodes.rationale: Production SQL-backed LocalSessionRepository must carry the SAME semantic guarantees as the in-memory reference, proven by a shared contract test suite run against both.

nodes.label: Orphan sessionId cleanup rule (${userId}--<random> prefix)
nodes.rationale: App generates sessionIds as ${userId}--<random>; deleteUserData additionally deletes orphan checkpoints/telemetry with that prefix to cover active sessions not yet saved, citing a WP11a concern.

nodes.label: WP12 Mobile Platform Integration Task
nodes.rationale: Implements location/motion providers, monotonic clock, permissions, preflight, lifecycle and native config per researched platform constraints; no device available so correctness is judged by current-SDK API usage, not runtime behavior.

nodes.label: Foreground-only location permission MVP
nodes.rationale: No background permission request in MVP: avoids Play policy friction and is not needed given keep-awake foreground-only sessions.

nodes.label: Mock-location sample rejection + diagnostics counter
nodes.rationale: Where the platform exposes a mocked-location flag (Android), the sample is rejected (not emitted) and counted, protecting timing integrity from GPS-spoofing dev tools.

nodes.label: WP12b iOS Platform Hardening Task
nodes.rationale: Harden the platform layer and app config for iOS as the PRIMARY target per ADR-0003, without regressing cross-platform (Android) behavior.

nodes.label: Reduced-accuracy detection -> PRECISE_LOCATION_OFF preflight failure
nodes.rationale: iOS lets users grant only reduced-accuracy location; since no temporary-full-accuracy API may exist in SDK 57, the ticket requires detecting reduced scope and surfacing an actionable preflight failure with Settings instructions rather than silently timing with degraded fixes.

nodes.label: GnssDiagnostics extended fields (interval histogram, accuracy p50/p95, reducedAccuracy flag)
WP13a Full UI Layer Task
nodes.rationale: Implements the complete production-quality UI against a mock session facade so the UI can be built and reviewed before the real pipeline exists; the facade is the swap point for later integration.

nodes.label: S7 ActiveDashboardScreen (dominant live delta, no map, no scrolling)
Long-press (2s) End Session control, no modals while timing
nodes.rationale: Prevents accidental touch from ending a live timing session; status changes render as inline banners instead of modal dialogs so the dashboard is never interrupted mid-lap.

nodes.label: composition.ts facade composition/swap point
nodes.rationale: App wires MockSessionFacade behind a single composition file specifically so the later integration work package can swap in the real facade by replacing exactly that file.

nodes.label: WP14 Full Integration Task
nodes.rationale: Replaces the mock session facade with the real production pipeline, wires persistence/recovery/watchdog, and proves offline standalone readiness -- this makes the app functionally complete.

nodes.label: Watchdog provider-restart mechanism (ADR-0003 amendment)
nodes.rationale: If no sample arrives for > watchdogTimeoutMs while active and not paused, the controller invokes a restartProvider callback and increments a diagnostic, so a stalled GNSS stream self-recovers instead of silently freezing the dashboard.

nodes.label: Checkpoint recovery on relaunch (ADR-0003 recovery flow)
nodes.rationale: On launch, an incomplete-session checkpoint offers recovery; restored laps are historical and the in-flight lap is marked invalid (RECOVERY) because tMono is per-launch and can never be compared across launches.

nodes.label: Static-bundle offline proof (TMR profile inlined, no fetch/fs at runtime)
nodes.rationale: The TMR profile must be a STATIC import so Metro inlines it into the bundle, and the app must never fetch or read from disk at runtime, so the app works fully standalone/offline on track.

nodes.label: DevReplayScreen wired to real fixtures via ReplayLocationProvider (10x)
WP4 Circuit Profile Schema Task
nodes.rationale: Versioned schema, validation, and migration framework so profile authoring (including future user-imported circuits) is safe and evolvable without breaking existing stored profiles.

nodes.label: makeTestProfile() / dev-test-ring synthetic fixture
nodes.rationale: A synthetic ~2km rounded-rectangle test circuit is required specifically so no real-circuit geometry is fabricated in this schema ticket; real-circuit authoring is a separate, provenance-controlled task.

nodes.label: WP4b TMR Profile Generator Task
nodes.rationale: A checked-in deterministic generator converts archived OSM extracts into a validated CircuitProfile JSON asset -- no hand-edited coordinates anywhere, so the profile is fully reproducible and auditable.

nodes.label: Determinism rule: fixed timestamps, no new Date(), regeneration byte-identical
nodes.rationale: createdAtUtc/updatedAtUtc are fixed literals and the generator must be re-runnable to a byte-identical asset, because provenance and auditability require the output to never silently drift.

nodes.label: S/F gate placement rule (pit-lane midpoint projected onto centerline)
Sector gate rule: perpendicular gates at 1/3 and 2/3 of totalLengthM
Pit entry/exit determination rule from travel-direction geometry
WP5 Geometry Core Task
nodes.rationale: Pure TypeScript domain geometry with exhaustive unit + property-based tests; a local tangent-plane approximation is acceptable and required for speed since circuits are <=~10km across.

nodes.label: WP6 Crossing Detector + Lap/Sector Timing Task
nodes.rationale: Pure logic timing engines with adversarial guards against duplicate crossings, GPS teleports, pit-lane laps, and low-quality windows -- time comes only from sample timestamps, never Date.now.

nodes.label: Rearm-distance guard (default 50m)
nodes.rationale: After a counted crossing, the gate is ignored until progress advances >=50m, specifically to kill duplicate/jitter crossings and stop-on-line oscillation.

nodes.label: Invalid-lap reason codes (SHORT_LAP, PIT_TRANSIT, LOW_QUALITY, PAUSE_GAP, REVERSE_TRAVEL, MISSED_SECTOR_GATE, DUPLICATE_SECTOR_GATE)
WP7 Quality/Matcher/Calibration Task
nodes.rationale: The Learn-lap calibration engine observes one complete recognition lap on a KNOWN circuit to establish alignment/confidence -- it never creates geometry.

nodes.label: Bounded bias estimation (1.5m-8m, trimmed-mean, session-level)
nodes.rationale: Lateral deviation alone is NOT an error because racing line != centerline; bias correction is applied only within a narrow bounded window and only when it measurably improves lateral tightness, so it can never silently over-correct.

nodes.label: WP8 Session State Machine Task
nodes.rationale: A pure, deterministic reducer: no Date.now, no timers, no randomness, no I/O -- all time arrives inside events so the machine is fully testable and checkpoint-serializable.

nodes.label: Illegal-event identity-return rule
nodes.rationale: Illegal events for a state are ignored by returning the SAME snapshot by reference rather than throwing, which keeps the reducer safe to call from any UI state and trivially testable.

nodes.label: WP9 Reference Lap / PB / Live Delta Task
nodes.rationale: Reference-lap resampling, personal-best acceptance rules, and the live-delta engine implement the binding PB replacement rules from contracts.md verbatim.

nodes.label: EMA display smoothing (alpha 0.3, raw value retained internally)
nodes.rationale: Smoothing is applied ONLY to the displayed delta so the UI reads steadily, while the raw internal value stays exact for correctness of estimatedLapMs and later comparisons.

nodes.label: Total closed-loop length 3706.488 m (matches asset totalLengthM exactly)
Clockwise direction match assertion (signed-area vs declared)
Sanity assertions (closed loop, S/F gate distance, sector 1/3-2/3, direction match -- all PASS)
Build unsigned iOS GitHub Actions workflow
nodes.rationale: Produces two CODE-SIGNING-DISABLED .ipa artifacts on a free macOS runner (no Apple Developer account, no secrets) so a user can re-sign them on Windows with Sideloadly and a free Apple ID.

nodes.label: TRACE Xcode scheme/workspace derivation rule
nodes.rationale: expo.name "mobile" in app.json is sanitized by @expo/config-plugins sanitizedName(); "TRACE" contains no characters that get stripped, so expo prebuild generates TRACE.xcworkspace with default scheme "TRACE" -- verified both by reading the sanitizer source and by this macOS CI job, since prebuild cannot run on the Windows dev machine.

nodes.label: CODE_SIGNING_ALLOWED=NO unsigned archive/package steps
nodes.rationale: No secrets are used anywhere in the workflow; the .ipa is unsigned by design so signing happens later, on the user's own machine, with their own free Apple ID via Sideloadly.

nodes.label: Circuit Timer project overview (advisory, recreational GNSS lap timer)
Verification commands (typecheck / test / lint / expo export)
ODbL / OpenStreetMap attribution requirement (way 488429454, way 488429716)
nodes.rationale: Circuit centerline and pit-lane geometry are derived from OpenStreetMap under ODbL 1.0; start/finish and sector gates are app-defined, not official, so attribution and non-official framing are load-bearing legal/ethical obligations, not cosmetic footer text.

nodes.label: Docs index (ADRs, algorithms, persistence-model, testing-and-replay, known-limitations)
Expo SDK 57 changed-docs verification notice
nodes.rationale: Instructs contributors to read the exact versioned Expo v57.0.0 docs before writing any code, because Expo APIs have changed and memory/training-data assumptions about Expo APIs are unreliable.

nodes.label: TMR geometry verification diagram (north-up centerline, pit lane, gates, direction arrows)
nodes.rationale: Renders the closed centerline (solid), pit lane (dashed), S/F gate, S1->S2 and S2->S3 sector gate markers, pit entry/exit markers, three travel-direction arrows at 10%/40%/70% progress, a north arrow, and a 500m scale bar -- a visual cross-check of the same measurements reported in the geometry verification report.

nodes.label: TRACE full logo (squircle container: metallic-silver T chassis + glowing amber apex racing curve)
nodes.rationale: Brand mark: a dark squircle icon container holds a metallic-silver "T" chassis outline with a glowing neon-amber gradient curve (telemetry apex/racing line motif) rendered with a layered Gaussian-blur glow filter -- the canonical reference the UI redesign and wordmark tickets restyle the app around.

nodes.label: TRACE logo mark (cropped, no container background)
nodes.rationale: Same metallic-silver T-chassis + glowing amber apex-curve artwork as trace_logo.svg but cropped/translated without the squircle background container, for use where a bare mark (not a full app icon) is needed.

nodes.label: Mobile App CLAUDE.md (Expo v57 docs pointer)
ADR-0002: TMR Geometry from OSM, Gates App-Defined
ADR-0004: iOS Without a Mac (Expo Go + EAS)
ADR-0005: Free Install Path (Unsigned CI ipa + Sideloadly)
iOS No-Mac Free Sideload Workflow Guide
Testing and Replay Doc (fixture catalog, determinism)
Baseline: Empty Repository at Project Start
CircuitProfile (schema-validated versioned circuit definition)
nodes.rationale: Every field is schema-validated (Zod strict) then structurally validated by validateProfile(); keyed on (circuitId, layoutId, layoutVersion) so corrected geometry never silently overwrites history.

nodes.label: Delta Sign Convention (negative = faster)
nodes.rationale: Binding convention: negative = faster than reference, positive = slower. Flows directly from rawDeltaMs = lapElapsedMs - referenceElapsedAt(distance); UI renders negative green, positive red.

nodes.label: Learn Lap Calibration
nodes.rationale: Answers one question only: is this session's GNSS trace trustworthy against the already-fixed profile geometry? Never creates or edits circuit geometry. Live auto-finish threshold (98% coverage) is deliberately above the 95% acceptance bar so direction-vote confidence, sample rate, and rejected-sample fraction firm up before the verdict; no stall timeout exists by design.

nodes.label: Bounded Bias Estimation
nodes.rationale: Two-pass trimmed least-squares (trim outer 10% residuals) against lateral residuals and centerline normals. Candidate applied only if 1.5-8 m magnitude AND p95 lateral spread improves to <=80% of before — smaller is noise, larger is an untrustworthy solve; the correction must measurably tighten spread, not just move it.

nodes.label: Coverage Bins (25 m monotonic centerline coverage)
nodes.rationale: Centerline divided into 25 m boolean bins; once covered, always covered (never regresses), with between-sample bin spanning unless the step is an implausible jump. Monotonicity is what makes the 98% auto-finish reachable exactly once.

nodes.label: Directed Gate Crossing Detection
nodes.rationale: Segment-segment intersection between the gate segment a->b and the motion segment prev->curr; direction is the sign of cross(gateVector, motionVector), only forward crossings count for timing; tCross is linearly interpolated between sample tMono values with IEEE-754 interior-value correction.

nodes.label: Gate Rearm Debounce (50 m)
nodes.rationale: After a counted forward crossing, further crossings of the same gate are suppressed until minRearmDistanceM (50 m) more unwrapped progress — turns five start-line jitter oscillations into exactly one counted crossing.

nodes.label: Monotonic Time Rule (incl. cross-launch rule)
nodes.rationale: All durations come from monotonic performance.now()-sourced tMono, never wall clock. Binding cross-launch rule (ADR-0003 §3): performance.now() origin resets per process launch, so tMono values from different launches are never comparable — recovery must never resume an in-flight lap timer, appending a zero-duration RECOVERY lap instead.

nodes.label: Reference Lap Resampling (10 m grid, monotone clamp)
nodes.rationale: buildReferenceLap resamples a completed lap onto a fixed 10 m distance grid; distances are monotone-clamped per sample and elapsed times re-clamped non-decreasing across the grid (belt-and-suspenders), anchored to (0,0) and (totalLengthM, durationMs). Fails INSUFFICIENT_COVERAGE unless >=95% of grid points fall inside the telemetry span.

nodes.label: PB Replacement Rules
nodes.rationale: Every rule must hold: same circuit/layout/layoutVersion identity, lap valid, quality floor good/degraded, not a pit lap, sectors complete and ordered, strictly faster, full telemetry with a full reference grid, provenance present, duration sanity within 1 ms. Replacement is atomic write-new-then-swap, evaluated immediately after every completed valid lap, never deferred to session end.

nodes.label: EMA Delta Display Smoothing (alpha 0.3)
nodes.rationale: displayedDeltaMs is an exponential moving average of rawDeltaMs (default alpha 0.3); on progress regression the EMA is held unchanged rather than updated; setReference/reset clear all state so every new lap and PB replacement starts the EMA fresh. Neutral display forced on staleness (>5 s gap), low confidence (<0.4), or unreliable quality.

nodes.label: Never-Fabricate Provenance Rules
nodes.rationale: Never hand-edit or invent coordinates; geometry must come from a real checkable source transformed deterministically by a checked-in generator. geometryStatus/sectorStatus must be honest not aspirational; license/attribution mandatory (surfaced in-app, not just in data); unknowns stated in confidenceNotes; better sources bump layoutVersion rather than mutating history.

nodes.label: Generator Script Pattern
nodes.rationale: Raw archived source in, structural assertions before trust, deterministic derivation with documented placement rules, a cross-check against an independently-verifiable fact (TMR: computed length within 1% of researched 3,708 m), and a versioned static output file statically imported by the app — never fetched at runtime.

nodes.label: layoutVersion Discipline
nodes.rationale: Exists so a corrected circuit definition never silently overwrites history: reference laps key on (circuitId, layoutId, layoutVersion) and shouldReplacePb refuses to compare across a layoutVersion mismatch. Bump on any meaningful gate/sector/centerline change; never mutate a shipped version in place.

nodes.label: Checkpoint Cadence (pause, lap complete, session end)
nodes.rationale: Checkpoints are written at exactly three points — pause, every completed lap, and session end (a terminal checkpoint so recovery never re-offers a saved session) — not per sample; a mid-lap crash can therefore lose telemetry back to the last boundary, which the recovery flow covers with a RECOVERY placeholder lap rather than fabricating a duration.

nodes.label: Checkpoint Recovery Flow
nodes.rationale: Historical laps restore verbatim into a fresh pipeline; a lap open at checkpoint time becomes a synthetic zero-duration RECOVERY lap (never a fabricated real time, because tMono is incomparable across launches); the session re-enters awaitingCalibration, with start('session') as the explicit resume-without-recalibrating path that dispatches a synthetic always-accepted calibration result.

nodes.label: Offline-First / No-Network Posture
nodes.rationale: Precise location is persisted locally only and never transmitted — a structural property, not a policy: zero fetch/XHR/axios/WebSocket call sites in either workspace, no analytics or crash reporting, and the circuit profile is statically inlined into the Hermes bundle (verified by bytecode scan), so no session-critical path touches the network.

nodes.label: Advisory-Recreational Disclaimer
nodes.rationale: The app is advisory and recreational, not an official or certified timing system — it never replaces organizer or FIM/FIA timing. Grounded in community-derived OSM geometry, app-defined gates, and the ~1 Hz GNSS precision ceiling.

nodes.label: Session Watchdog (5 s sample-gap restart)
nodes.rationale: expo-location SDK 57 does not expose activityType/pausesUpdatesAutomatically on the foreground watch path, so Core Location's default auto-pause risk is mitigated by restarting the watch subscription whenever no sample arrives for >5 s while active and unpaused, incrementing a watchRestarts diagnostic. Binding on WP14 integration.

nodes.label: Unsigned CI ipa + Sideloadly Free Install Path
nodes.rationale: Expo Go is retired for SDK 57 and EAS device builds require a paid Apple account, so the free path is a GitHub Actions macOS runner building unsigned Release and dev-client .ipa files, signed on Windows via Sideloadly with a free Apple ID — 7-day signature expiry and 3-app limit accepted; re-signing with the same bundle id (app.circuittimer.tmr) preserves app data.

nodes.label: Deterministic Fixture Catalog (15 adversarial scenarios)
nodes.rationale: Every fixture wraps a deterministic kinematic drive around the real TMR centerline with a seeded 32-bit LCG PRNG (never Math.random), synthetic monotonic tMono (never Date.now), frozen non-enumerable metadata, and the real profile rather than a synthetic test track — bit-for-bit reproducible per seed.

nodes.label: ReplayHarness / runSessionPipeline
nodes.rationale: Batch entry point that drives fixture samples through the full production pipeline (quality -> matcher -> crossings -> state machine -> timing -> delta) via the same SessionPipelineCore the live controller uses, so the two consumers can never independently diverge on pipeline order.

nodes.label: Transilvania Motor Ring (circuit, Cerghid, Romania)
nodes.rationale: 3.708 km clockwise circuit at 46.43528N 24.42694E, opened November 2018, largest racing venue in Romania. OSM way 488429454 (centerline, 150 nodes, ~3706 m) and way 488429716 (pit lane) are the geometry source; official start/finish, pit, and sector definitions are not publicly available.

nodes.label: Corridor Width Wiring Gap (profile 15 m vs live 20 m)
nodes.rationale: The profile's corridorWidthM (15 m for TMR) is used only by profile validation; CalibrationEngine and TrackMatcher independently default to 20 m and are never overridden in the composition root, so production calibration and matching run at 20 m, not the profile's value.

nodes.label: SessionController (production orchestrator)
nodes.rationale: Consumes LocationProvider + MonotonicClock + LocalSessionRepository + RuntimeProfile + userId and composes the same five pipeline engines the replay harness uses via shared SessionPipelineCore — no duplicated wiring between batch replay and live operation. Owns calibration flow, arming, per-lap checkpointing, immediate PB evaluation, the watchdog, and checkpoint recovery.

nodes.label: Hold to End Session Button (red outline, hold-to-confirm)
Delta-to-Reference Timing Concept
nodes.rationale: The screen dedicates its central visual band to a horizontal delta bar labeled 'SECONDS VS. REFERENCE' rather than showing only absolute lap time: at speed a rider can parse a left/right gain-loss bar far faster than digits, so the design prioritizes relative pace against a reference lap for glanceability.

nodes.label: Glanceable Dark High-Contrast UI Design
nodes.rationale: Pure-black background, very large monospaced timer digits, minimal chrome, color-coded status (green GNSS pill, amber active sector, red destructive action) and a hold-to-confirm gesture on 'End Session' — all choices consistent with an on-track/handlebar-mounted use case: readable in sunlight at a glance, and protected against accidental session termination.

nodes.label: Blueprint Construction-Grid Motif
nodes.rationale: The background layer is drawn as a technical-drawing construction grid: two concentric circles around a small center point, a dashed vertical centerline, a solid horizontal baseline, and dashed diagonal guides forming a triangle apex at the top of the outer circle, all in light blue line-work on a pale blue field. The motif communicates precision/measurement — fitting for a lap-timing app — and its near-monochrome low-contrast styling keeps the layer safe under Android adaptive-icon masking and parallax cropping, where outer regions may be cut off.

nodes.label: Blue Chevron Apex Mark
nodes.rationale: Upward-pointing chevron (caret/apex shape) reads as the letter 'A' apex and as a track-apex/summit motif appropriate for a lap-timing app; centered on a plain white field with generous margins so the Android adaptive-icon mask can crop safely without clipping the mark.

nodes.label: Glossy Blue Gradient Treatment
nodes.rationale: Saturated blue at the top fading to a pale ice-blue toward the lower leg tips, with soft inner glow and rounded stroke ends — gives the flat glyph depth and a modern iOS/Android 'liquid glass' feel without extra shapes.

nodes.label: TRACE Chevron Brand Mark (Monochrome Android Icon)
Android Adaptive Icon Monochrome Layer (Material You Themed Icon)
TRACE Brand Identity
nodes.rationale: The icon encodes the app's dual nature: a static engineered letterform (metallic chiseled T, precision/hardware) overlaid by a dynamic glowing racing line (amber neon trace, motion/telemetry). The trace follows and diverges from the T's own contour like a driven lap line diverging from the ideal line, visually stating 'lap timing over a fixed track'. Dark near-black squircle maximizes contrast and reads as a premium motorsport/night-mode aesthetic on iOS home screens.

nodes.label: Dark near-black background with amber/yellow accent palette
TRACE brand mark (racing line traces the letter T)
TRACE App Icon (neon T on dark rounded square)
Dark Brand Theme (near-black background, amber accent)
Metallic T Letterform
nodes.rationale: Dark gunmetal, beveled/chamfered 3D letter T with light edge highlights; anchors the mark as the initial of the app name TRACE and reads cleanly on transparent/dark backgrounds.

nodes.label: Amber Neon Racing-Line Trace
nodes.rationale: Glowing amber/yellow neon tube with outer glow that runs up the T's stem, loops through a hairpin curve over the crossbar, and doubles back down — a visual pun: the 'trace' is a driver's racing line through a hairpin corner, encoding the lap-timing purpose of the app directly in the mark.

nodes.label: TRACE Lap-Timing App Brand Identity
nodes.rationale: Brand identity for the TRACE lap-timing app: dark metallic base plus amber accent, motorsport night-race aesthetic; rasterized from trace_logo_mark.svg for use as the mobile app's logo asset.
